title: Fair price for iOS
body:
⭐⭐

I genuinely appreciate the functionality and sleek design of the Things app, deserving a solid 4 stars in that department. However, the pricing strategy leaves me baffled. While the 89 DKK for iOS feels justified, charging an exorbitant 399 DKK for the Mac version — over 4 times the iOS price — is hard to justify. It feels disproportionate and, honestly, a bit senseless.

author: MrRonnie0982

title: Just really, really good!
body:
Yes, it’s as good as they say :-) Do the tutorial project, and you’ll be off in no time - and never look back, I promise you! This is really going to help me in my daily life, thank you Cultured Code! 

Ohh, and THANK YOU for making this a one-time paid app, and not a monthly subscription. I don’t mind paying a little more for quality work, but I’m tired of being ripped-off by subscription-based “services” that add nothing but cloud-sync and web-access you never use - good on you for resisting this guys! 👍😇

One wish though: I’d love to be able to do basic formatting using a few fonts (monospaced and a few carefully selected serif and sans serif options) plus bold, italic and so on. Nothing wild, just a few options 🙂 

Or, actually - perhaps just the option of choosing a different interface font or size, I’d really just like a bit smaller font for lists and views, to cram a bit more info into the inbox and other views? Just an idea 😎

author: MsMadsen

title: Very good, but a few significant flaws..
body:
Although I find the app rather un-intuitive when it comes to distribution of tasks on the various time related lists, it works well once you get to know the logic and the app is simple and stable to use. 

The thing that’s driving me crazy is the lack of a list that shows EVERY task regardless of the settings on it, and a list that shows important/high priority tasks across any other setting. 

The app doesn’t look at the “Important” tag with higher priority -eg moving it to the top of the list it’s on- but just as a tag, which defeats the purpose of tagging something as important. 

I want to commit to this app as my task manager (buying the expensive desk top version), but holding back for now because of this.

title: Focus is on interface.  Best for new users.
body:
There is not much you can do with this app yet. So expect to miss some features you find in other apps. Read the developers homepage before you buy. Perhaps this is just right for you. It might be the case if you have simple needs and are new to this type of app.  It was not for me: You cannot attach files to a note. You cannot take or attach a photo to a note. When you use the "import from Wunderlist" feature" this app do not import other than simple text. Then it adds a link to the note in Wunderlist where you have to keep attached files and photos. So now you have to use both apps!!! The app uses its own cloud service. No iCloud. 
I got a quick response from the developer after my initial review. I had missed that the app actually includes repeating tasks. Nicely done but hard to find because the interface is made to be simple. So I added two stars to my review and changed the text.

title: Great to do list, Great for GTD
body: I love Things 3 finally a to do list that is simple to use, but have the features and power that you need in a to do list. Things are the best tool for getting things done without spending to much time on the actual to do list. I have used Omnifocus, Wunderlist, todoist, and many morethese are all great but things 3 simplicity makes me chose their solution. Well done on this update. The only missing part from my side is to be able access this from Windows that would be awesome as many of us is using this at work.
